1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 d6 4.Bc4 h6 5.d4.strategy: Hits the g5 pawn before the bishop reaches g7 to protect h6: if Black ignores it, hxg5 hxg5 opens the h-file and Rxh8 wins the undefended rook. Black has to answer on the kingside at once, while the c1-bishop still eyes f4 and White keeps the initiative.

Protects the h6 pawn at the end of the chain f4-g5-h6, so after hxg5 hxg5 the rooks simply trade. The bishop also looks down the long diagonal at White's d4 pawn. Black keeps the extra pawn, and White must make up for it with the centre and the initiative.
